note_out: Greek religion included spirits and anthropomorphic gods, but no source established the proposed historical transformation.
Aristotle's hylomorphic soul is documented; descent from prehistoric animism is not.
Aristotle explicitly criticizes Plato's transcendent Forms and makes forms predicates of primary substances.
Pythagorean influence was limited; SEP calls inferring it from Plato's mathematics a serious mistake and does not derive his core Forms from it.
Heraclitean and Stoic logos are a standard historical connection, though the opened pages did not explicitly state direct influence.
Britannica explicitly connects Greek logos with Christian theology and John's identification of Christ as the incarnate Word.
The Hebrew Bible, including Genesis, constitutes the major portion Christians call the Old Testament.
SEP describes Aquinas's systematic reworking of Aristotelianism within Christian commitments.
Aquinas is explicitly presented as a foundational scholastic advocate integrating philosophy with revealed Christian theology.
Descartes styled himself a Christian philosopher and pursued the Church-backed project of proving the soul's immateriality.
SEP explicitly describes occasionalism's textbook role as a response to Cartesian mind-body interaction.
Leibniz found Cartesian interaction unintelligible and replaced it with pre-established harmony.
La Mettrie extends machine language to feeling animals and humans while making soul a material brain function.
Locke's founding empiricist polemic rejects innate ideas and supplies an experience-based alternative to Cartesian nativism.
Berkeley starts from Lockean ideas in the mind and argues toward immaterialism and esse est percipi.
Kant explicitly credited remembering Hume with interrupting his dogmatic slumber and redirecting his philosophy.
SEP documents Leibniz's influence and the conventional account of Kant navigating Leibnizian rationalism and Humean empiricism.
SEP explicitly presents Kant's thinking-for-oneself and public reason as expressions of Enlightenment commitments.
Bentham's calculative ethics belongs to the late Enlightenment, but no opened source explicitly established this broad developmental link.
Hegel's project arose from Kantian critical philosophy and sought to systematize and complete transcendental idealism.
SEP explains Hegelian idealism as knowledge becoming self-knowledge through the identity of thinking and being.
Oxford describes Dawkins's gene's-eye view as a later shift within evolutionary theory founded by Darwinian natural selection.
The article explicitly identifies Darwin's between-tribe reasoning as the essential logic of modern multilevel selection.
Rockefeller describes Neural Darwinism as neuronal-group selection resembling natural selection in evolution, though using different mechanisms.
Levin documents cooperative cellular agency and body-building, but no source tied this specifically to historical cell theory.
The source explicitly calls McGinn the contemporary continuator of du Bois-Reymond's unknowability claim.
Chalmers explicitly discusses whether consciousness is causally inert, finding epiphenomenalism coherent but undesirable.
Husserl adopted and transformed Brentano's descriptive, object-directed account of experience into phenomenology.
Archival research lists multiple Brentano courses Freud attended from 1874 through 1876.
The source discusses James's teaching laboratory and Wundt's permanent research laboratory in psychology's institutionalization as laboratory science.
Skinner explicitly said radical behaviorism restores introspection and does not deny self-observation; the note fits Watson better than Skinner.
Husserl explicitly acknowledged Kant's legacy when calling phenomenology transcendental and broadened Kantian analysis of experience.
The source traces enactivism through phenomenology and identifies Husserl's lived body, kinaesthesia, and bodily 'I can' as enactive ideas.
IEP connects Russell's discovery to Cantor's theorem and the unrestricted comprehension associated with naïve set theory.
Russell's 1902 letter explicitly communicated the paradox that undermined Frege's Grundgesetze.
Wittgenstein acknowledged Frege and inherited his function-argument analysis and conception of logic's relation to language.
Frege advised Wittgenstein to study with Russell, which he did at Cambridge from 1911.
SEP uses Peano Arithmetic as the standard arithmetic theory to which incompleteness applies.
Gödel's 1931 paper is explicitly titled for formally undecidable propositions of Principia Mathematica and related systems.
Gödel's theorems are generally taken to block Hilbert's original completeness and finitary consistency program.
Brouwer attempted to reconstruct Cantorian set theory but rejected completed higher number classes as incompatible with constructive intuitionism.
SEP explicitly chronicles the foundational dispute between Brouwer's intuitionism and Hilbert's formalist program.
The historical study presents Frege's rigorous semantics as a close precursor to Tarski's formal truth theories.
Frege explicitly framed Begriffsschrift as first steps toward Leibniz's general characteristic and calculus of reasoning.
Turing explicitly says his Entscheidungsproblem result is quite different from Gödel's; calling it incompleteness merely restated for machines conflates distinct theorems.
Turing introduced his machines to prove that Hilbert and Ackermann's Entscheidungsproblem has no general effective solution.
Turing proved equivalence between lambda-definability and Turing computability.
SICP uses Scheme, whose first-class procedures derive from lambda calculus, but no single reliable opened source stated the complete link.
Von Neumann knew Turing's universal machine, but historians dispute whether it influenced his stored-program architecture.
The Royal Society records Turing's 1952 paper The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis.
Stanford's AI history says Turing's 1950 essay inspired AI and anticipated machine intelligence and learning before Dartmouth.
SEP defines hypercomputation as yielding functions that are not Turing-computable.
Quantum Turing machines compute no additional functions; their prospective advantage is efficiency.
Solomonoff explicitly says Shannon's information theory profoundly shaped his induction ideas through probability and information packing.
The original Dartmouth proposal names Shannon among its four originators.
